atoms.reference: A university consortium of more than 219 research libraries (2024) under shared governance, administered by the University of Michigan; executive director Mike Furlough (Wikipedia).

evidence.record_quote: HathiTrust Digital Library is a large-scale collaborative repository of digital content from research libraries , administered by the University of Michigan .
As of 2024, members include more than 219 research libraries
across the United States, Canada, and Europe, and is based on a shared governance structure.
The executive director of HathiTrust is Mike Furlough,
HathiTrust was founded in October 2008 by the twelve universities of the Committee on Institutional Cooperation and the eleven libraries of the University of California .

atoms.reference: A large-scale collaborative repository of digital content from research libraries, restricting access where a work's copyright or permission status cannot be determined, and for users outside the United States to works published outside it from 1896 (Wikipedia).

evidence.record_quote: HathiTrust Digital Library is a large-scale collaborative repository of digital content from research libraries , administered by the University of Michigan .
if we cannot determine the copyright or permission status of a work, we restrict access to that work until we can establish its status.
access is also restricted for users outside the United States to works published outside the United States after and including 1896.

atoms.reference: More than 18 million volumes, 6.7 million in the US public domain (September 2024), digitized via Google Books and the Internet Archive and locally by libraries (Wikipedia).

evidence.record_quote: In September 2024, HathiTrust comprised more than 18 million volumes, including 6.7 million in the public domain in the United States.
Its holdings include content digitized via Google Books and the Internet Archive digitization initiatives, as well as content digitized locally by libraries.

atoms.reference: Full-text search across the whole repository; the Shared Print Program's retention of almost 18 million volumes for 25 years; lawful access for member libraries' users to copyright digital copies in place of the physical books; its use of books scanned by Google held fair use, search and accessibility for the visually impaired grounds for finding it transformative (Wikipedia).

evidence.record_quote: HathiTrust provides a number of discovery and access services, notably, full-text search across the entire repository.
The HathiTrust Shared Print Program is a distributed collective collection whose participating libraries have committed to retaining almost 18 million monograph volumes for 25 years
for users of HathiTrust member libraries to obtain lawful access to copyright digital materials in place of the corresponding physical books held by the same library.
A federal court ruled against the Authors Guild in October 2012, finding that HathiTrust's use of books scanned by Google was fair use under US law.
which found that providing search and accessibility for the visually impaired were grounds to consider the service transformative and fair use
